newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.

text.p: Yields ended lower supported by a weaker-than-expected Philly Fed while the trade in crowns was very calm.
The Swedish yield curve flattened markedly and the T-bill rates were little changed.

"The Swedish CPI resulted in a belief that reporate hikes may come sooner, maybe already in Q4 rather than in Q2 1998", one dealer said and added that long bonds are in demand while players are selling short bonds.
"I think we will see several hikes and that's why people are selling short bonds and T-bills become uninteresting", he said.
CPI was 0.5 percent month-on-month compared to expected 0.2 pct.
American statistics presented a mixed picture and there are differing views on what the Fed will do on May 20.
"The market focus is on FOMC meeting 20th May. I don't think that they will do a rate hike but you never know", one dealer said.

The six-month T-bill rate was two basis points up at 4.19 percent and the 10-year bond yield fell three basis points to 6.91 pct. The crown firmed marginally to 4.4640 crowns against the mark versus 4.4700 crowns on Wednesday.
